analysis.evidence: In הוּא הָיָה גִבֹּר צַיִד (“he was a mighty hunter”), הוּא is the subject of הָיָה (“was”). It refers to Nimrod, named again in כְּנִמְרֹד (“like Nimrod”).
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person masculine singular personal pronoun.

analysis.evidence: הָיָה links הוּא, referring to Nimrod, with the predicate גִבֹּר צַיִד, “a mighty hunter.” The saying in the second half of the verse repeats that description of Nimrod.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third-person masculine singular, agreeing with the subject הוּא.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: צַיִד specifies hunting as the activity in which Nimrod excels. The phrase גִבֹּר צַיִד means “a mighty hunter” and recurs in the saying “like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before YHWH.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular adjective in the construct state, used substantivally with צַיִד.

analysis.evidence: גִבֹּר צַיִד describes Nimrod as a mighty hunter. צַיִד names the activity in which he excels, and the proverb repeats the same description later in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase גִבֹּר צַיִד.

analysis.evidence: In גִבֹּר צַיִד לִפְנֵי יַהְוֶה, the phrase לִפְנֵי יַהְוֶה describes Nimrod as a mighty hunter in Yahweh’s sight. The saying in the second half of the verse repeats the phrase.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לִ־ combines with פְנֵי, the plural construct of פָּנִים, a common noun of both genders. Together they function as a preposition governing יַהְוֶה.
analysis.sense: before, in the presence of (a person, Yahweh)

analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: עַל כֵּן יֵאָמַר means “therefore it is said” and introduces the proverbial comparison beginning כְּנִמְרֹד, “like Nimrod.”
analysis.morphology: Niphal imperfect, third person masculine singular, used impersonally to express customary speech.
